name: ES Playbook
tagline: The slow-money instrument of the futures props: measured range statistics, the ORB evidence that's harsher on ES than on NQ, the gap-and-overnight mechanics that bite funded accounts, and the case for ES when the trailing drawdown is the binding constraint.
summary: ES is the deepest, tightest book in index futures — about 1.2 million contracts a day in the cash session — and the market most often recommended to traders who keep losing on NQ wicks. The measurements support the temperament claim and complicate the strategy claim: raw opening-range breakouts fail on ES too (a costs-on 18-year test called the textbook version untradeable), while the *statistical* substrate is friendlier — the first hour carries over half the day's range, only ~4% of days stay inside it, and genuine two-way chop is rare. What ES genuinely offers a funded account is a stop-size profile: with 2026's ~70-point average daily range, the same $200–400 of planned risk fits 4–12-point stops at MES, with dozens of losing streaks of room left on a $2,000 floor. This guide covers the data, the session clock with its firm-specific flat-by times, overnight gap mechanics, and the ES-vs-NQ decision as the sources actually frame it.
oneLiner: Trade the open's resolution of the overnight range with confirmation closes, size MES at a fraction of the risk unit, and treat the trailing floor — not the contract's volatility — as the whole game.
keyQuote: More than five points is a great day, and more than ten means you crushed it. Five to ten points a day, taken consistently, is the business.
keyQuoteSource: veteran ES scalper's public journal, on income expectations

stats.label: Days staying inside the first hour

lead: ES rewards the same discipline NQ punishes at speed — the evidence for which setups work is stricter than the marketing, and the risk arithmetic is where ES wins.
highlights: Textbook ORB fails on ES after costs in the harshest test — but 30-min range + close-confirmation continuation hits ~70% in the statistics.
The overnight high/low gets taken out by the cash session on ~60% of days — mark it, trade the reaction, don't predict fills.
Only ~4% of sessions stay inside the opening hour — the IB-break statistics are even stronger than on NQ.
Weekend repricing is a 49-hour window with 7% limits — the Sunday reopen does Monday's work.
Firm flat-by times vary from 4:10 to 4:59 PM ET — know yours before holding through a close.
At 10-point stops, MES risks $50 per contract — the instrument that lets a $2,000 floor breathe.
